title: Lena and the Promise
premise: Tamsin Amberdale, a marine biologist who fled his family's coastal hotel empire after a broken engagement, hires Lena, a festival coordinator he barely knows, to pose as his girlfriend at the Amberdale family reunion. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens as Lena uncovers the truth about why Tamsin left, and as her own secret, she's quietly negotiating to sell the family's beloved shoreline to developers, threatens everything. When the deception is exposed at the festival's climax, Tamsin must choose between the duty of silence that protected his family and the truth that could win Lena back. He chooses truth, publicly, and asks her to stay past the last train, past the festival's end, into a real beginning.
about_author: Petra Ravensworth is the pen name of a former tide-pool tour guide who wrote her first romance on the back of a marine survey form. She lives in a seaside cottage with two rescue cats and a stubborn belief that every last train can be missed for the right reason.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On a research boat, Tamsin counts nesting turtles and avoids calls from his mother about the family reunion. A chance collision with Lena, a festival coordinator, leaves him flustered and intrigued. The emotional beat is guarded loneliness: a man measuring life in data points because feelings once cost him everything.

chapters.title: The Reunion Clause
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cornered by his mother's ultimatum, come to the reunion or lose his say in the family trust, Tamsin impulsively asks Lena to be his fake girlfriend. She names a price: he volunteers at her harbor festival all week. The beat is wary negotiation, two strangers striking a deal neither can afford emotionally.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Talk
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. First rehearsals: Tamsin learns Lena's festival world, Lena learns his family's history with the cove. Their practiced couple story keeps slipping into real laughter. The beat is tentative warmth, the fake beginning to feel inconveniently easy.

chapters.title: The Amberdale Table
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The reunion's first dinner: sharp-eyed aunts, a smug cousin, and Tamsin's ex-fiancée, Vivian, seated deliberately across the table. Lena improvises brilliantly, then catches a flicker of real pain in Tamsin's eyes. The beat is protective tenderness, Lena realizing she cares more than the contract allows.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A late-night walk; Tamsin tells Lena about the broken engagement, how his family chose the hotel's image over him, and why he counts turtles instead of returning calls. Lena almost confesses her secret about the shoreline sale. The beat is intimacy earned through truth, with one truth still held back.

chapters.title: Dessert and Detonations
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Mid-reunion, the couple act feels too real by dessert, until Vivian publicly questions Lena's identity and Lena's developer contact calls at the worst moment. She deflects, but Tamsin notices. The beat is rising tension: the fake romance solidifying as her hidden stake in the cove begins to crack the surface.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin discovers the sale documents with Lena's signature pending, the cove where he counted turtles, sold by the woman he's falling for. He confronts her; she explains she took the job before knowing him, and the money was for her father's care. He walks away. The beat is heartbreak and betrayal, the midpoint collapse.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Devastated, Lena tears up the deal and digs into the developer's file, discovering he plans to raze the turtle nesting grounds and frame the Amberdales for it. She races to warn the family but is turned away at the gate. The beat is lonely resolve: choosing loyalty to the cove and to Tamsin over her own safety.

chapters.title: Festival of Small Fires
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the festival's climax, the developer's scheme goes public; Vivian, of all people, corroborates Lena's warning. Tamsin must choose: defend his family's silence or stand before the whole reunion and declare the truth, about the cove, his exile, and Lena. The beat is the climax: public truth as an act of love.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The festival ends, the cove is saved, and the last train pulls out without Lena aboard, because Tamsin asked her, in front of everyone, to stay. On the empty platform, they begin again without a contract. The beat is resolution and belonging: second chances, finally, for people with better timing.
